A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniEval and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices. The methods and experiments can be matched despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original human quality inspection, evaluator validation, and retriever/generator experiments, including Tables 3–5 and topic/task analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional topic-by-task results for the auto-generated evaluation set.

M1.justification: The GPT-4-based classification, generation, quality inspection, human correction, and fine-tuned Qwen evaluator pipeline remains the same. Appendix C supplies detailed instructions for this existing procedure without establishing an algorithm or model change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same financial corpus sources, 16 topics, five QA tasks, and auto-generated and human-annotated evaluation sets. Expanded task instructions and additional breakdowns do not establish new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same evaluator, retriever, generator, and closed-book comparators. V2's Llama3.1 table label agrees with v1's experimental prose; it does not establish a replacement baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 adds an inapplicable value of -1 for HAL and NAC and explicitly excludes -1 cases from metric aggregation. Six human-test subset counts increase by one between v1 Figure 10 and v2 Figure 11. These are reported protocol/count revisions; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 extends the joint topic-by-task diagnostic analysis with auto-generated-test matrices in Figures 12, 14, 16, and 18. Existing topic-only, task-only, and human-test matrix analyses are retained. No new ablation or robustness study is reported.

E5.justification: The evaluator agreement reporting using accuracy and kappa remains unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds auto-test matrix result entries and revises six human-test counts. Tables 3–5 and matched existing plots retain their numerical results, allowing for rounding. Attribution of Figure 12 is unclear: Figures 12 and 14 label different auto-test matrices as the same Qwen configuration, so no model-specific performance improvement can be inferred.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, assumptions, derivations, or proofs. The topic-task Cartesian-product construction is retained; the metric revisions concern operational evaluation rules.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain matrix-based financial RAG evaluation, automated generation with human inspection, retrieval and generation assessment, and rule-based plus LLM-based metrics. The main claims about acceptance rate, evaluator accuracy, and uneven RAG capabilities are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds limitations concerning corpus accessibility/licensing, resulting distribution bias and generalizability, and limited human data for evaluator training. Section 4.1 also adds model size as an explanation for GTE's performance, alongside the retained explanation involving LLM pretraining.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds detailed task requirements, GPT-4 prompt templates, input/output schemas, quality criteria, and a human annotation/correction flowchart absent from v1. V2 also newly specifies five retrieved documents and the Rouge-L implementation. These substantially expand procedural documentation without proving implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to the GPT-4 technical report, LoRA, and Tan et al.'s data annotation/synthesis survey, and explicitly credits DomainRAG for the task selection. The overall positioning and comparison with financial benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction, methods, results discussion, and conclusion are rewritten. V2 separates retriever and generator results, introduces a dedicated matrix-visualization subsection, and reorganizes the appendix into statistics, supplementary results, and instructions.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redraws diagrams, heatmaps, and bar charts, changing colors, labels, numeric annotations, and legends. It relocates retained plots between the main text and appendices and adds matrix plots, task tables, a flowchart, and prompt displays. Table 2 also drops its average-length column.

improvement.justification: The new procedural documentation, clearer experimental organization, and explicit limitations improve transparency and usability. These gains outweigh limited reporting defects, including unexplained count revisions and inconsistent model references: Section 4.5 describes Figure 4 as DeepSeek although its caption identifies Llama, and Figures 12 and 14 duplicate the Qwen attribution for different matrices.
